summary: A novel method for the template-free synthesis of magnetic-metal nanorods (NRs) of Co and Ni using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) is developed. The process involves the use of NH3 plasma mixed with a suitable amount of SiH4 as a reactant, resulting in the spontaneous formation of vertical NRs. The lengths of the NRs are controlled by the number of PE-ALD growth cycles. The study confirms the magnetic anisotropy of Co NRs due to shape anisotropy.
evidence: A novel fabrication method of Co and Ni metal nanorods (NRs) without catalyst or template, based on the spontaneous formation of NRs during plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD) is developed. ... The same conditions used in Co NR growth were applied to the PE-ALD of Ni with bis(dimethylamino-2-methyl-2-butoxo)nickel(II) (Ni(dmamb)2). ... SQUID magnetometer measurements confirmed the magnetic anisotropy of Co NRs due to shape anisotropy.
